analysis: The MultiDAE trial achieved host validation macro HR@10 of 0.5650: +0.0013 versus the previous 0.5637, but −0.0087 versus the reported best 0.5737. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.625, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.600, Electronics 0.390, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.645. Electronics remains the weakest category, improving from the previously reported 0.380. The deterministic bottleneck produced a small observed improvement over the latest trial, but did not recover the best result. These results alone do not establish that variational regularization caused the earlier shortfall; expert metrics and selected fusion weights were not included in the supplied host result. The run succeeded and consumed 474.35 allocated GPU-seconds.
code_summary: Per-category SASRec + MultiDAE ensemble, retaining the 'vae' member key and MultVAE compatibility class. MultiDAE uses L2-normalized binary full-history inputs, 0.5 input dropout, a 256-unit tanh encoder, deterministic 64-dimensional latent projection, and a 256-unit tanh decoder to item logits. It trains with multinomial reconstruction loss only, without sampling, KL loss, or residual bypass. SASRec retains two attention blocks, 64-dimensional embeddings, a gated prefix-preference component, and cross-entropy over one positive plus 64 unseen negatives. Each expert starts from seed 42 and independently selects its checkpoint by validation HR@10, breaking ties by NDCG@10. Frozen expert ranks are fused using reciprocal rank constant 60 and the unchanged five-weight grid. Metadata identifies MultiDAE; strict reload, deterministic scoring, and exported predictor agreement checks are included for all four dataset routes.
